question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: The text must consist of EXACTLY 16 characters, every one of them in HEX16; otherwise -> throws. Nothing is trimmed or normalized first: uppercase digits, fewer or more than 16 digits, any whitespace anywhere (including one final line feed), a prefix, a sign, a separator and non-ASCII digits all throw. The throw's message is not part of the contract. CITED FIDELITY package

The result is the binary64 value whose bit pattern is the 64-bit integer the digits denote, reinterpreted without any numeric conversion: 8000000000000000 is negative zero, 7ff0000000000000 and fff0000000000000 are the infinities, and every pattern with all exponent bits set and a non-zero fraction is a NaN.
